subject: Clarifying our 'no training' guarantee and retention edge-cases
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@fintegrity.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@fintegrity.com>

Subject: Clarifying data use — do you train on our data?

Hi Markus / Laura,

Quick question from our compliance team as they review the draft DUA: Fintegrity needs a firm statement that Redwood does not use customer content (API inputs, uploaded files, or inference outputs) to train or improve shared model weights unless the customer explicitly opts in.

Two follow-ups:
- Can you confirm the statement covers both Hosted Redwood API and Redwood Dedicated?
- What about transient caches (inference KV cache, prefix caches) and any retention for logs/backups — how long do those stick around and where?

We'd like to capture precise language for our security questionnaire. If you have a one-page summary or a CSV with retention buckets, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Sarah

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarifying data use — do you train on our data?

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear questions. Below is the concise assurance and then a short breakdown of retention/edge cases. I've attached our SOC2 summary and a CSV that maps retention buckets.

Short assurance (suitable for questionnaire):
"Redwood Inference does not use customer-provided content (API inputs, uploaded files, or inference outputs) to train, fine-tune, or update any shared production model weights unless the customer has provided explicit, documented opt-in (e.g., a signed Data Use Addendum). This applies to Hosted (Redwood API) and Dedicated deployments. For Private deployments managed by the customer (VPC/on-prem), Redwood does not access customer data for any training purposes."

Retention and operational notes (summary):
- Inference KV/prefix cache: ephemeral by design; per-request KV cache is kept in-memory on the serving node and is not persisted to long-term storage. A small, short-lived in-memory cache may exist for up to 6 hours in normal operation to improve latency; it is automatically evicted per our cache policy.
- Request logs (request metadata, timestamps, routing info): default retention 30 days for hosted tiers; can be configured for Dedicated under contract. Logs do not contain raw input/output payloads by default unless the customer enables full request logging for debugging or support.
- Full request payloads (if enabled by customer for debugging): stored encrypted at rest and retained for 30 days by default; customers can request earlier deletion.
- Backups & snapshots (infra snapshots kept for DR): rotated and retained for up to 90 days; deletion requests are processed as described below but may be subject to recovery windows for DR processes.
- Audit logs (security/audit trails): retained for 365 days to meet compliance and incident response needs.
- Aggregated telemetry (metrics/usage): kept indefinitely in anonymized, aggregated form and cannot be mapped back to raw customer content; used to tune system performance only.

Exceptions / legal holds:
- We will retain data beyond the stated retention periods if required by law, regulatory investigation, or court order.

Deletion process (how we handle a customer deletion request):
1) Customer submits deletion request via Console or Support portal (we provide a deletion token and request ID).
2) We schedule deletion across active stores and mark the request in our audit queue.
3) Primary data stores (S3) will have objects removed within 48 hours; metadata and indices are scrubbed within 72 hours.
4) Backups/snapshots: we mark snapshots for purge and perform secure deletion within 90 days (shorter windows can be negotiated in contract).
5) We return a deletion completion receipt with affected object counts and trace IDs.

If you want contract language, suggest the short assurance above verbatim. I've attached: SOC2-summary-2027.pdf and data_retention_table.csv which lays out the buckets.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through any technical specifics.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: SOC2-summary-2027.pdf, data_retention_table.csv)

Thanks, Markus — that helps a lot. Couple of narrow technical clarifications before we finalize language:
1) KV/prefix cache: you mentioned up to 6 hours in-memory. Can you confirm that those caches are never written to durable storage (S3, DB) in Hosted and Dedicated?
2) Snapshots/backups: when you say "secure deletion within 90 days" how do you handle immutable snapshots in cloud provider backups? Is the 90-day window the max and can Fintegrity request a faster purge for covered datasets?
3) If a customer enables full request logging for debugging, is there an easy toggle to revoke that and delete previously captured payloads?

Also, our legal team wants to avoid language that leaves ambiguity about "used to tune system performance" — can you supply a sentence that explicitly states what "aggregated telemetry" excludes (i.e., it excludes raw customer prompt/content)?

Appreciate it — happy to book a call if easier.

-Sarah

Hi Sarah — jump in from Product Compliance to add the precise clarifications you asked for and the contract-friendly phrasing.

Answers to your numbered questions:
1) KV/prefix cache durability: Confirmed — KV and prefix caches used for inference are never persisted to durable object storage in normal operation for Hosted and Dedicated. They live in RAM on serving nodes; when a node restarts or the cache evicts, the content is lost. We do not intentionally materialize those caches to S3 or long-term DBs.
2) Snapshots/backups: 90 days is our standard maximum purge window for DR snapshots, but customers may negotiate a shorter maximum in the DUA (we can commit to 30 days for covered datasets in contract). Note that some cloud-provider level immutable backups may impose a minimum retention; in those rare cases we surface the delta and coordinate expedited purge where feasible.
3) Full request logging toggle: Yes — for Hosted customers who have enabled full payload logging, we provide an admin toggle to disable future capture and a one-click deletion flow that marks captured payloads for deletion; processed deletions produce an audit receipt. Historical copies in backups are handled per the snapshot purge timeline above.

Safe sentence for the questionnaire on aggregated telemetry: 
"Redwood collects aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry (metrics such as token counts, endpoint latency percentiles, and error rates) for service quality and infrastructure optimization. This aggregated telemetry explicitly excludes raw customer inputs and outputs and cannot be reconstituted into customer content."

Next steps:
- I've attached a short deletion playbook image (deletion_playbook.png) that maps the flow and timelines.
- If Fintegrity would like a contractual guarantee, we can add the 30-day snapshot purge for their covered datasets and include the toggle behavior for full logging in the DUA addendum.

Would you like to schedule a call this week to finalize wording?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
